title: A Conversation With the Architect of Trump's New Trade War

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在早上4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空的七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个平底锅就能做好的菜，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您理解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受特别优惠：nytimes.com slash subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: President Trump says he's going to announce so-called reciprocal tariffs on every country with duties placed on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统表示，他将宣布对所有对美国征收关税的国家征收所谓的对等关税。

sentences.en: With less than a month in office, we're just hours into a new trade conflict.
sentences.zh: 距离上任还不到一个月，一场新的贸易冲突在短短几小时内就爆发了。

sentences.en: President Trump has pursued more trade actions against adversaries and allies than all the trade measures he took in his entire first term.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统针对竞争对手和盟友采取的贸易行动，比他整个第一任期内采取的所有贸易措施还要多。

sentences.en: Tariffs ordered by President Trump went into effect at mid-
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统下令征收的关税在半夜正式生效——

sentences.en: Canada and Mexico will be among the hardest hit by these tariffs.
sentences.zh: 加拿大和墨西哥将是受这些关税打击最严重的国家之二。

sentences.en: These tariffs more than triple what was done during the first term.
sentences.zh: 这些关税是第一任期内所作所为的三倍以上。

sentences.en: And there's one man guiding it all.
sentences.zh: 而这一切背后有一位主导者。

sentences.en: President-elect Trump choosing Peter Navarro for a top economic position in his next administration.
sentences.zh: 当选总统特朗普选择彼得·纳瓦罗在其下一个政府中担任重要经济职位。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Anna Swanson on how Peter Navarro rose to become one of Trump's key advisors and why he thinks tariffs will usher in a new era of American prosperity.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安娜·斯旺森将讲述彼得·纳瓦罗如何崛起成为特朗普的关键顾问之一，以及他为什么认为关税将开启美国繁荣的新时代。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, February 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月18日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hi, Anna.
sentences.zh: 嗨，安娜。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: I wanted to talk to you because you covered President Trump in his first term and you focused a ton on international trade.
sentences.zh: 我想和你谈谈，因为你在特朗普的第一任期内报道过他，并且把大量精力放在了国际贸易上。

sentences.en: So I figured you would be the right person to talk to and help me understand this key advisor, Peter Navarro,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你是合适的人选，能跟我聊聊并帮我理解这位关键顾问彼得·纳瓦罗，

sentences.en: who's been advising Trump on all of these tariff policies that we've been hearing about recently.
sentences.zh: 他一直在就我们最近听到的所有关税政策向特朗普提供建议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I met Peter Navarro when I was covering trade policy in Trump's first term.
sentences.zh: 我是在特朗普第一任期报道贸易政策时认识彼得·纳瓦罗的。

sentences.en: And he's an interesting person because he had a very unusual journey to the White House.
sentences.zh: 他是一个有趣的人，因为他通往白宫的经历非常不寻常。

sentences.en: And he had views about trade in China that were considered pretty unconventional and unpopular.
sentences.zh: 他对贸易和中国的看法曾被认为是相当非正统且不受欢迎的。

sentences.en: But over time, these views have become one of the driving forces of Trump's trade policy.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，这些观点已经成为特朗普贸易政策的驱动力之一。

sentences.en: So I'm pleased to see you after four long years of exile.
sentences.zh: 很高兴在长达四年的流放后见到你。

sentences.en: So recently, I went to see him again with two colleagues from The Daily.
sentences.zh: 所以最近，我和《每日新闻》的两位同事又去拜访了他。

sentences.en: I actually listen to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 其实我有听《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I have it on my podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我的播客里有它。

sentences.en: We met him at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building, which is just west of the White House.
sentences.zh: 我们在艾森豪威尔行政办公楼见到了他，该大楼就在白宫西侧。

sentences.en: We're going to turn to the right here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里向右转。

sentences.en: And we sat down with him in his office to understand how he came to have these ideas about trade and tariffs.
sentences.zh: 我们在他的办公室里坐下来，了解他是如何对贸易和关税产生这些看法的。

sentences.en: So you want us here?
sentences.zh: 所以你想让我们来这儿？

sentences.en: And now that he's in the role that he's in, what his ideas could mean for the country.
sentences.zh: 而现在他担任了这个职务，他的想法对国家意味着什么。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Navarro, you are synonymous with Donald Trump and his agenda.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦罗博士，你简直就是唐纳德·特朗普及其政治议程的代名词。

sentences.en: But not all that long ago, you were a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 但不久前，你还是一名民主党人。

sentences.en: So tell us that story.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这段经历吧。

sentences.en: Where does that story start?
sentences.zh: 这个故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: It went from being kind of a Democrat to being a Trump Republican.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上的民主党人变成了特朗普式的共和党人。

sentences.en: And the reality is that there's not much difference between that.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，这两者之间其实没有太大区别。

sentences.en: The traditional Democratic Party was a lot like MAGA in that it was the party of the working class, American manufacturing, blue-collar workers.
sentences.zh: 传统的民主党在很多方面很像MAGA（让美国再次伟大），因为它是工人阶级、美国制造业和蓝领工人的政党。

sentences.en: The goal of that party, at least what it said it was, was to increase the real wages and prosperity of blue-collar workers.
sentences.zh: 那个政党的目标，至少它所宣称的目标，是提高蓝领工人的实际工资和繁荣程度。

sentences.en: And I was very comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 我对这一点感到非常适应。

sentences.en: I grew up in a single-family household with my mom.
sentences.zh: 我和妈妈在一个单亲家庭长大。

sentences.en: We had a hard life.
sentences.zh: 我们过得很艰难。

sentences.en: And I identify to this day with the working class.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我依然对工人阶级有强烈的认同感。

sentences.en: So when you started talking, what did you learn?
sentences.zh: 当你开始交谈时，你学到了什么？

sentences.en: So he talked about being raised by a single mom, how he was a latchkey kid.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了自己是由单亲妈妈抚养长大的，以及他曾经是个挂着钥匙的孩子。

sentences.en: He also loved school.
sentences.zh: 他也热爱学校。

sentences.en: And he did well.
sentences.zh: 而且他表现得很好。

sentences.en: And he goes on to Tufts University.
sentences.zh: 接着他进入了塔夫茨大学。

sentences.en: And after he graduated in the 1970s, he's thinking he wants to see what the world is like and travel a little bit.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代毕业后，他想着去看看世界是什么样的，到处旅行一下。

sentences.en: I became really intrigued by Thailand.
sentences.zh: 我对泰国产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: And one day, as I was thinking that maybe I should go there.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我正想着或许我应该去那里。

sentences.en: And then one day, kind of randomly, he's walking around the Berkeley campus.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，有点偶然地，他在伯克利校园里闲逛。

sentences.en: And this guy asked him, hey, want to go to Thailand?
sentences.zh: 有个家伙问他，嘿，想去泰国吗？

sentences.en: And I looked over, and it was the Peace Corps table.
sentences.zh: 我转头一看，那是和平队（Peace Corps）的桌子。

sentences.en: And that guy happened to be recruiting for the Peace Corps.
sentences.zh: 而那个人正好在为和平队招募人员。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I had to say yes because of the synchronicity of the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 由于这一切的巧合，我不得不答应。

sentences.en: I don't want to get too Californian on you.
sentences.zh: 我不想显得太具有加州风格。

sentences.en: But that was an interesting moment.
sentences.zh: 但那是一个有趣的时刻。

sentences.en: And so Navarro decides to go.
sentences.zh: 于是纳瓦罗决定前往。

sentences.en: Peace Corps, I feel like that's a really unusual stop along your way to becoming tariff czar.
sentences.zh: 和平队，我觉得这是你成为关税沙皇之路上的一个非常不寻常的停靠站。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He says he wanted to learn about different cultures and got to travel a lot around Asia.
sentences.zh: 他说他想了解不同的文化，并且有机会在亚洲各地旅行。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole ability to see the world from outside the United States, it makes you very humble.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从美国以外的视角看世界的这种能力，会让你变得非常谦逊。

sentences.en: And when I came back, it motivated me to go into policy.
sentences.zh: 当我回来时，这激励我走向了政策领域。

sentences.en: And when he came back, he ended up at Harvard studying government and economics in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 他回来后，于80年代进入哈佛大学研究政府与经济学。

sentences.en: He finished his PhD.
sentences.zh: 他完成了博士学位。

sentences.en: He moves out to Southern California.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了南加州。

sentences.en: And he starts teaching economics and public policy at UC Irvine.
sentences.zh: 并开始在加州大学尔湾分校教授经济学和公共政策。

sentences.en: And then he decides to run for mayor of San Diego.
sentences.zh: 然后他决定竞选圣迭戈市长。

sentences.en: My only goal as mayor was to address the problems of traffic ingestions, the overcrowded schools, the awful sewage system.
sentences.zh: 我当市长的唯一目标就是解决交通拥堵、学校过度拥挤以及糟糕的污水系统等问题。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a populist campaign just at the local level on a different set of issues.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场针对不同议题的、仅限地方层面的民粹主义竞选。

sentences.en: I mean, I sometimes joke I was like mini Trump before Trump.
sentences.zh: 我有时开玩笑说，我在特朗普之前就像个微型特朗普。

sentences.en: He loses that election.
sentences.zh: 他输掉了那场选举。

sentences.en: And over the next several years, a couple of huge economic policy shifts happen that really shape his thinking.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，发生了几次重大的经济政策转变，深刻地塑造了他的思维方式。

sentences.en: First in 1994 comes NAFTA, the North American Free Trade Agreement.
sentences.zh: 首先是在1994年，北美自由贸易协定（NAFTA）出台。

sentences.en: And this is a really important moment for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这对美国经济来说是一个非常重要的时刻，

sentences.en: economy because this was the first time that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为这是美国

sentences.en: was engaging in a free trade agreement with a developing country, Mexico.
sentences.zh: 首次与一个发展中国家——墨西哥——签订自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: And then in 2001, China enters the World Trade Organization, this other big moment in trade that really shifts the politics of trade in America.
sentences.zh: 然后在2001年，中国加入了世界贸易组织，这是贸易领域的另一个重大时刻，真正改变了美国的贸易政治。

sentences.en: So it sounds like you have these two big moments where America is really becoming much more globalized in its manufacturing processes.
sentences.zh: 听起来你有这两个重大时刻，当时美国的制造流程正变得越来越全球化。

sentences.en: You've got NAFTA, where it's signing agreements with places like Mexico and opening itself up to other countries.
sentences.zh: 你有了NAFTA，它与墨西哥等地签署协议，并向其他国家开放自己。

sentences.en: And then you've got this moment when China joins the World Trade Organization, which really brings China onto the world main stage in a way that it hadn't been before.
sentences.zh: 然后你迎来了中国加入世贸组织的时刻，这以前所未有的方式将中国带上了世界主舞台。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's after these big policy shifts when Navarro starts to see something happening with his students that bothers him.
sentences.zh: 正是在这些重大政策转变之后，纳瓦罗开始注意到他的学生身上发生了一些让他感到困扰的事情。

sentences.en: I was the macroeconomist teaching business students how to forecast the economy.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一名宏观经济学家，教商务专业的学生如何预测经济。

sentences.en: And in about 2002 and 2003, I began to notice that the business students who were in the fully employed program were losing their jobs.
sentences.zh: 大约在2002年和2003年，我开始注意到那些在职项目的商科学生正在失去他们的工作。

sentences.en: And it was like, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 当时的情况就像是，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: He's trying to figure out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他试图弄清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: And he lands on something that he calls the China price.
sentences.zh: 然后他锁定了一个他称之为“中国价格”的概念。

sentences.en: And what's that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So he's observing this strange ability for Chinese firms to offer prices that are so much lower than other competitors.
sentences.zh: 他观察到中国企业拥有提供远低于其他竞争对手价格的奇异能力。

sentences.en: 50% lower prices.
sentences.zh: 价格低50%。

sentences.en: And he's saying that is starting to put U.S.
sentences.zh: 他说这开始让美国制造商陷入破产。

sentences.en: manufacturers out of business.
sentences.zh: 制造商业倒闭。

sentences.en: So he does a study to try to understand just how they're getting their prices so low.
sentences.zh: 于是他做了一项研究，试图弄清楚他们是如何把价格压得这么低的。

sentences.en: It wasn't simply low wages.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为低工资。

sentences.en: So one way companies could get their prices low is by paying their workers lower wages.
sentences.zh: 公司降低价格的一种方法是通过向工人支付较低的工资。

sentences.en: But Navarro finds that China is doing a lot more than that.
sentences.zh: 但纳瓦罗发现中国做的远不止于此。

sentences.en: Like currency manipulation, like counterfeiting and piracy, the use of pollution havens, things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如汇率操纵、假冒伪劣和盗版、利用污染避难所以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he's so troubled by this that he ends up writing three books on China.
sentences.zh: 他对此深感困扰，以至于最终写了三本关于中国的书。

sentences.en: The first was called The Coming China Wars.
sentences.zh: 第一本叫做《即将到来的对华战争》。

sentences.en: It just got skewered in the financial times.
sentences.zh: 它刚在《金融时报》上遭到痛斥。

sentences.en: That book gets panned.
sentences.zh: 那本书遭到了严厉批判。

sentences.en: Do you remember anything from the skewering?
sentences.zh: 你还记得被痛斥时的什么内容吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it's just, you know, it's just radical, crazy guy, you know, this kind of thing, right?
sentences.zh: 哦，也就是，你知道的，就是激进、疯狂的家伙，诸如此类的话，对吧？

sentences.en: And I thought, look, these people don't get it, except among all of the corporations and unions and plain old folk that were getting just hammered by that.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，听着，这些人根本不懂，但在所有那些遭到沉重打击的企业、工会和普通百姓中间，

sentences.en: It's like, OK, let's keep going on this.
sentences.zh: 情况就像是，好的，让我们继续这样做。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: People read books, but not a lot of them anymore.
sentences.zh: 人们看书，但现在没多少人看了。

sentences.en: So let's do the movie.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来拍电影吧。

sentences.en: And then he also creates a documentary, which is narrated by Martin Sheen.
sentences.zh: 然后他还创作了一部纪录片，由马丁·辛担任旁白。

sentences.en: And it was the same kind of reaction, Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞的反应也差不多。

sentences.en: And it's like, oh, you're exaggerating stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像是，噢，你们在夸大其词。

sentences.en: Ana, how would you characterize Navarro's view of all of this?
sentences.zh: 安娜，你如何评价纳瓦罗对这一切的看法？

sentences.en: Is his assessment of what China is doing fair?
sentences.zh: 他对中国所作所为的评估是公正的吗？

sentences.en: He's right that a lot of people agree now that the Chinese government was not playing by international trade rules.
sentences.zh: 他说得对，现在很多人都同意中国政府没有遵守国际贸易规则。

sentences.en: But even if they were, I think the entry of basically a billion people into the global economy would have been a huge shock either way.
sentences.zh: 但即使他们遵守了，我认为基本上有十亿人口进入全球经济，无论如何都会是一个巨大的冲击。

sentences.en: And it ends up being kind of complicated in terms of who benefited and who loSt.
sentences.zh: 结果在谁受益、谁受损方面变得有点复杂。

sentences.en: OK, so let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Tell me what some of the benefits are firSt.
sentences.zh: 先告诉我有哪些好处。

sentences.en: So the first benefit is that you do have a lot of Chinese people lifted out of poverty.
sentences.zh: 首先带来的好处是，确实有很多中国人的生活摆脱了贫困。

sentences.en: So hundreds of millions of Chinese people who are moving out of poverty into the middle class.
sentences.zh: 数以亿计的中国人正摆脱贫困，迈入中产阶级。

sentences.en: And then you have basically the American standard of living today created.
sentences.zh: 然后，基本上创造了如今的美国生活水平。

sentences.en: You know, how many people do you know who love Costco, who love to buy inexpensive things off of Amazon?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你认识多少人喜欢去开市客（Costco），喜欢在亚马逊上买便宜的东西？

sentences.en: A lot of that is made possible by this China price, by Chinese factories making cheap goods.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分要归功于这个“中国价格”，归功于中国工厂制造的廉价商品。

sentences.en: But there were definitely a lot of downsides as well.
sentences.zh: 但显然也有很多负面影响。

sentences.en: So you have a lot of U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多美国工厂倒闭了，

sentences.en: factories going out of business because they can no longer compete with the cheap prices that Chinese firms are offering.
sentences.zh: 因为它们再也无法与中国企业提供的低价竞争。

sentences.en: And you have millions of U.S.
sentences.zh: 经济学家发现，在这个过程中，有数百万个美国

sentences.en: manufacturing jobs that were destroyed in that process, economists have found.
sentences.zh: 制造业工作岗位被摧毁。

sentences.en: And I don't think they anticipated just how hard the people on the losing end would be hit.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们预料到处于失败一方的人们会受到多么沉重的打击。

sentences.en: There was this assumption that people who lost their jobs to trade could be helped to move to find other jobs or go through retraining programs that would give them, you know,
sentences.zh: 当时有一种假设，即因贸易而失业的人可以得到帮助去寻找其他工作，或者参加再培训计划，这些计划将为他们提供，你知道的，

sentences.en: even better jobs in this new economy.
sentences.zh: 在这场新经济中甚至更好的工作。

sentences.en: And they didn't anticipate, I think, that this transition was a lot more disruptive and painful.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他们没有预料到这种转型会带来如此巨大的混乱和痛苦。

sentences.en: And the pain was really localized and vivid and sharp, particularly in the industrial Northeast and Midwest,
sentences.zh: 这种痛苦非常具体、鲜明且剧烈，尤其是在工业化的东北部和中西部地区，

sentences.en: where people now are really hurting because they don't have factory employment anymore.
sentences.zh: 那里的人们现在正饱受痛苦，因为他们再也没有工厂的工作了。

sentences.en: And economists have found that then other problems follow, like drug addiction.
sentences.zh: 经济学家发现，随之而来的是其他问题，比如药物成瘾。

sentences.en: And these are all things that Peter Navarro was focused on, too, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些也都是彼得·纳瓦罗关注的问题。

sentences.en: When I did my Death by China movie, I went to Dayton.
sentences.zh: 当我拍摄《致命中国》这部纪录片时，我去了代顿。

sentences.en: I saw the people who would otherwise be in factories walking around with shopping carts, stealing copper out of homes and buildings, whatever they could,
sentences.zh: 我看到那些本该在工厂工作的人推着购物车四处游荡，从房屋和建筑里偷铜，只要能偷的都偷，

sentences.en: and then going and using the money to get high.
sentences.zh: 然后用这些钱去买毒品吸食。

sentences.en: It really does sound like Peter Navarro is ringing the alarm bell on China kind of well before a lot of other people are.
sentences.zh: 听起来彼得·纳瓦罗确实比许多其他人早得多地对中国敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: How does he actually get attached to Donald Trump, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，他是怎么和唐纳德·特朗普搭上线的呢？

sentences.en: So Trump at this point has been complaining about China and its trade practices for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普在那个时候已经抱怨中国及其贸易做法很长一段时间了。

sentences.en: President Trump, the way we intersected was through an interview, interestingly enough, that he did for the Los Angeles Times in 2011.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统，我们产生交集是通过一次采访，很有意思的是，那是他2011年为《洛杉矶时报》接受的采访。

sentences.en: At one point, Trump is asked by the L.A.
sentences.zh: 有一次，《洛杉矶时报》问特朗普：

sentences.en: Times, what are some of your favorite books on China?
sentences.zh: “关于中国，你最喜欢读哪些书？”

sentences.en: And he proceeded to do something I'm not sure I could even do.
sentences.zh: 接着他做了一件连我自己都不确定能不能做到的事。

sentences.en: He listed his top ten books by title and author.
sentences.zh: 他按书名和作者列出了他心中的前十本书。

sentences.en: And I was number six, the coming China wars.
sentences.zh: 而我是第六名，《即将到来的对华战争》。

sentences.en: And he mentions one of Peter Navarro's books.
sentences.zh: 他提到了彼得·纳瓦罗的一本书。

sentences.en: So they start corresponding and...
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始通信，然后……

sentences.en: One thing led to another and...
sentences.zh: 一件事接着另一件，然后……

sentences.en: Ultimately, then candidate Trump decides to bring Navarro on to his campaign.
sentences.zh: 最终，当时的候选人特朗普决定让纳瓦罗加入他的竞选团队。

sentences.en: What I try to do is see problems and solve them.
sentences.zh: 我试着做的就是发现问题并解决问题。

sentences.en: And the problem I saw crystal clear is the unfair trade that was driving up these large trade deficits and shutting down our factories and creating just all sorts of misery for blue-collar workers.
sentences.zh: 我清晰地看到的问题是，不公平的贸易推高了这些巨额贸易逆差，迫使我们的工厂倒闭，并给蓝领工人带来了各种各样的苦难。

sentences.en: Trump wins the presidency, and Navarro is given a job in the administration working on trade policy.
sentences.zh: 特朗普赢得总统大选，纳瓦罗在政府中得到了一份负责贸易政策的工作。

sentences.en: But he's still kind of an outsider.
sentences.zh: 但他在某种程度上仍然是个局外人。

sentences.en: There are a lot of other more influential advisors in the administration at that point who are opposed to the idea of imposing broad tariffs on foreign products.
sentences.zh: 当时政府中还有许多其他更有影响力的顾问，他们反对对外国产品征收广泛关税的想法。

sentences.en: And so you come to a point where, you know, most of the other advisors are saying to President Trump, we can't do that.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现，你知道的，大多数其他顾问都在对特朗普总统说，我们不能那样做。

sentences.en: You know, we shouldn't impose tariffs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们不应该征收关税。

sentences.en: It was always the same, like Mnuchin and Cohn and Kudlow and all these people.
sentences.zh: 情况总是这样，比如姆努钦、科恩、库德洛和所有这些人。

sentences.en: They just didn't buy in.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不买账。

sentences.en: And the defining moment for me in terms of when I finally was able to begin doing what the president wanted me to do was about four months in, and he made the famous,
sentences.zh: 对我和我最终能够开始做总统希望我做的事情而言，决定性的时刻大约在大约四个月后，他打出了那个著名的，

sentences.en: where's my Peter call.
sentences.zh: “我的彼得在哪里”的电话。

sentences.en: It's like he's sitting around with these guys four months in, nothing's happening at all.
sentences.zh: 就像他在四个月后和这些人坐在一起，什么进展也没有。

sentences.en: And he goes, where's my Peter?
sentences.zh: 然后他说：“我的彼得在哪里？”

sentences.en: I go over there, and I have this, like, battle with Cohn and whatever.
sentences.zh: 我走过去，和科恩之流吵了一架什么的。

sentences.en: And then some months later, I'm able, with Wilbur Ross, to get the steel and aluminum tariffs in, and Cohn leaves like a crying little baby in a huff.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，我和威尔伯·罗斯成功推出了钢铁和铝关税，而科恩像个哭泣的小婴儿一样气冲冲地走了。

sentences.en: And Navarro prevails, and he helps to draft tariffs on China and on steel and aluminum from countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦罗获胜了，他协助起草了针对中国以及世界各国钢铁和铝产品的关税。

sentences.en: So when Trump and Navarro leave office in 2021, what exactly had they accomplished in terms of the trade relationship with China?
sentences.zh: 因此，当特朗普和纳瓦罗在2021年卸任时，他们在与中国的贸易关系方面究竟取得了什么成就？

sentences.en: So they had really changed the American terms of trade with the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实改变了美国与世界其他地方的贸易条款。

sentences.en: They had imposed a lot of tariffs on things like metals and washing machines and over $300 billion of products coming in from China.
sentences.zh: 他们对金属、洗衣机以及价值超过3000亿美元的中国进口产品征收了大量关税。

sentences.en: And they had also signed a trade deal with China and reworked the North American Free Trade Agreement into a new deal.
sentences.zh: 他们还与中国签署了一项贸易协议，并将《北美自由贸易协定》重新谈判成了一项新协议。

sentences.en: But then there's an interesting wrinkle to this story.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事还有一个有趣的转折。

sentences.en: So Trump's orbit has changed a lot through the whole first term.
sentences.zh: 所以在整个第一个任期内，特朗普的团队发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: New advisors have come in.
sentences.zh: 新的顾问进来了。

sentences.en: They get fired.
sentences.zh: 他们被解雇了。

sentences.en: You know, people are in and out very quickly.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人员进出非常频繁。

sentences.en: But Peter Navarro, even though he's sometimes sidelined, is there the whole time.
sentences.zh: 但彼得·纳瓦罗，尽管有时被边缘化，却一直都在。

sentences.en: And when the January 6th hearing comes, Navarro is called to testify.
sentences.zh: 当1月6日的听证会到来时，纳瓦罗被传唤作证。

sentences.en: And he shows his loyalty to Trump by refusing to hand over his notes.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝交出自己的笔记，以此向特朗普显示忠诚。

sentences.en: And then he is sent to prison for four months for failing to honor the subpoena.
sentences.zh: 然后他因未能履行传票而被判入狱四个月。

sentences.en: So just to clarify, I went to prison not because I didn't want to cooperate with an investigation,
sentences.zh: 所以为了澄清一下，我入狱不是因为我不想配合调查，

sentences.en: but because it was my duty as a senior White House official to refuse to appear when issued an unlawful congressional subpoena.
sentences.zh: 而是因为作为白宫高级官员，当收到非法的国会传票时，拒绝出庭是我的职责。

sentences.en: That case is being litigated.
sentences.zh: 这个案子正在审理中。

sentences.en: It was unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 这很不幸。

sentences.en: They put me in prison until they should have waited until my appeal ran its course.
sentences.zh: 他们把我投进监狱，本该等到我的上诉走完法定程序。

sentences.en: But I want to be really clear about why I went to prison.
sentences.zh: 但我想要非常明确地说明我为什么入狱。

sentences.en: I was defending the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我在捍卫宪法。

sentences.en: Now, to your point.
sentences.zh: 好，回到你的观点。

sentences.en: And he gets out of prison on the day of the Republican National Convention.
sentences.zh: 他在共和党全国代表大会当天出狱。

sentences.en: And he flies directly from prison to the RNC to give a speech.
sentences.zh: 他直接从监狱飞到共和党全国代表大会发表演讲。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: This morning I did walk out of a federal prison in Miami.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我确实走出了迈阿密的一所联邦监狱。

sentences.en: Joe Biden and his Department of Injustice put me there.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登和他的“不公正部”把我弄到那里去的。

sentences.en: Wow, that is quite an image.
sentences.zh: 哇，那真是一个极具冲击力的画面。

sentences.en: And we know what happens next.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Trump, who is somebody who obviously prizes loyalty very much, wins the election, returns to office, and he brings Peter Navarro back with him.
sentences.zh: 显然非常看重忠诚的特朗普赢得了大选，重返白宫，并把彼得·纳瓦罗带了回去。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this time he is even more empowered to totally transform America's trade relationships.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他被赋予了更大的权力来彻底改造美国的贸易关系。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“连接”字谜游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作“拼字蜜蜂”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So from the review of my book, there's been a steady evolution of thought amongst the public, even on Wall Street, about what I've been saying, what the president has been saying,
sentences.zh: 所以从对我的书的评论来看，公众甚至华尔街的思想一直在稳步演变，关于我一直在说的，关于总统一直在说的，

sentences.en: what others in our camp have been saying.
sentences.zh: 关于我们阵营中的其他人一直在说的。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm mainstream now.
sentences.zh: 我想我现在已经进入主流了。

sentences.en: That's scary.
sentences.zh: 这真可怕。

sentences.en: So, Ana, now that we understand how Peter Navarro formed his worldview about trade with China, let's talk about his tools for bringing back manufacturing jobs to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，阿娜，既然我们已经了解了彼得·纳瓦罗是如何形成他对华贸易世界观的，让我们来谈谈他将制造业工作带回美国的工具。

sentences.en: And those tools are tariffs.
sentences.zh: 这些工具就是关税。

sentences.en: Tell us about how Navarro makes the case for tariffs.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲纳瓦罗是如何为关税进行辩护的吧。

sentences.en: So, Peter Navarro believes that tariffs are a very important tool to balance out America's trading relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以，彼得·纳瓦罗认为关税是平衡美国贸易关系的一个非常重要的工具。

sentences.en: That, as we talked about, countries like China have been cheating international rules by making products more cheaply than they should and stealing intellectual property.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，像中国这样的国家通过以低于应有成本的价格制造产品和窃取知识产权来欺骗国际规则。

sentences.en: And basically, they're putting out goods that American businesses just can't compete with.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们生产的商品是美国企业根本无法竞争的。

sentences.en: And so, American businesses need kind of a shield from those products.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国企业需要某种针对这些产品的盾牌。

sentences.en: And that shield is tariffs.
sentences.zh: 而这个盾牌就是关税。

sentences.en: How exactly is it a shield?
sentences.zh: 它到底是怎么成为盾牌的？

sentences.en: Well, a tariff is a charge on a good when it comes over the border.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关税是对跨越边境的商品征收的费用。

sentences.en: So, if companies are making their products outside the United States and they want to sell them inside the United States, they pay that extra fee.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果公司在美国境外制造产品并希望在美国境内销售，他们就要支付这笔额外费用。

sentences.en: So, the thinking is tariffs will incentivize companies to make their products inside the United States so they don't have to pay that fee.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们的想法是，关税将激励公司在美国境内制造产品，这样他们就不必支付这笔费用了。

sentences.en: But what does Navarro say about the criticisms that are often cited of using tariffs?
sentences.zh: 但对于人们经常提到的对使用关税的批评，纳瓦罗是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Like, Trump himself has acknowledged on social media that tariffs could lead to higher prices, for example, for consumers.
sentences.zh: 比如，特朗普本人曾在社交媒体上承认，关税可能会导致价格上涨，例如对消费者而言。

sentences.en: And in the U.S., just to point out, we just went through a period of super high inflation.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，顺便指出一下，我们刚刚经历了超级高的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And that was really, really painful for people.
sentences.zh: 这对人们来说真的是非常、非常痛苦。

sentences.en: So, I asked him about that, and he was pretty clear about his position.
sentences.zh: 所以我问了他这个问题，他对自己的立场相当明确。

sentences.en: Tariffs do not cause inflation when they're imposed by the largest market in the world.
sentences.zh: 当关税由世界上最大的市场实施时，它们不会引起通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And that has been demonstrated by the fact that we aggressively imposed tariffs during the first term.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一任期内大力征收关税的事实已经证明了这一点。

sentences.en: We had zero inflation as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果我们实现了零通胀。

sentences.en: He said that tariffs will not hurt consumers.
sentences.zh: 他说关税不会伤害消费者。

sentences.en: So, I did want to push back on some of the economics of tariffs and also get your response.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实想对关税的一些经济学原理提出反驳，并听听你的回应。

sentences.en: So, you know, first, there were quite a few studies that showed that American consumers did bear the brunt of the China tariffs, that much of that cost was passed through.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，首先，有相当多的研究表明，美国消费者确实承担了对华关税的冲击，很大一部分成本被转嫁了。

sentences.en: But then, secondly, even more basically, I mean, isn't...
sentences.zh: 但其次，甚至更根本的是，我的意思是，难道没有……

sentences.en: Hang on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Stay with that.
sentences.zh: 坚持这个话题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 我们这样吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, who were the studies by?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些研究是谁做的？

sentences.en: You know, a lot of very prominent economists.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多非常著名的经济学家。

sentences.en: Prominent economists.
sentences.zh: 著名的经济学家。

sentences.en: New York Fed, but other academic economists as well.
sentences.zh: 纽约联储，但也有其他学术经济学家。

sentences.en: All the ones that were wrong about Trump.
sentences.zh: 所有在特朗普问题上犯错的人。

sentences.en: You know, like the biggeSt...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像最大的……

sentences.en: Ones that you don't believe in and that you kind of felt...
sentences.zh: 你所不相信的，而且你觉得……

sentences.en: But I think it's fair, Ana, for you to go back and look at those analyses who said it and then look what they said, for example, when Trump came into office
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，阿娜，你回头去看看那些分析报告，看看是谁说的，然后再看看他们说了什么，比如当特朗普上任时，

sentences.en: and how they predicted there would be chaos, recession, inflation, stagnation.
sentences.zh: 以及他们如何预测会有混乱、衰退、通胀、停滞。

sentences.en: That has never happened.
sentences.zh: 那从来没有发生过。

sentences.en: I think my point here is that the academic community can't be trusted to critique Trump economics.
sentences.zh: 我想我的观点是，学术界在批判特朗普经济学时是不可信的。

sentences.en: And they have a credibility problem because they've been crying this wolf.
sentences.zh: 他们存在信誉问题，因为他们一直在“狼来了”。

sentences.en: They did it all through the first term.
sentences.zh: 他们在整个第一任期内都是这么做的。

sentences.en: None of that happened.
sentences.zh: 那些都没有发生。

sentences.en: They're just wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们就是错的。

sentences.en: We're right.
sentences.zh: 我们是对的。

sentences.en: They're wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们是错的。

sentences.en: End of story.
sentences.zh: 故事结束。

sentences.en: And you feel that the American people are on your side with that assessment that economists don't know what they're talking about?
sentences.zh: 你觉得美国人民在“经济学家根本不知道他们在说什么”这一评估上是站在你这边的吗？

sentences.en: It's the American people who've borne the brunt of this for going on, what, 40 years now.
sentences.zh: 是美国人民一直在承受这一切的冲击，持续了，什么，现在已经40年了。

sentences.en: How many times do you have to be told by politicians and corporate flax that this free trade stuff
sentences.zh: 你还得被政客和企业帮办说多少次这种自由贸易对你有好处，

sentences.en: is good for you and then you lose your job and your community falls down around you for you to stop believing them?
sentences.zh: 然后你失业了，你的社区在你身边崩塌，你才会停止相信他们？

sentences.en: I mean, that's why Trump got elected in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是特朗普在2016年当选的原因。

sentences.en: Setting economists and think tanks aside, I mean, even sort of common sense, right?
sentences.zh: 抛开经济学家和智库不谈，我的意思是，甚至还有某种常识，对吧？

sentences.en: So tariffs work by raising the price of foreign goods.
sentences.zh: 所以关税的作用是通过提高外国商品的价格来起作用的。

sentences.en: And when the price of foreign goods go up, you know, that is what encourages people to buy domestic goods.
sentences.zh: 当外国商品价格上涨时，你知道的，这正是鼓励人们购买本土商品的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't that the way that tariffs work?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道关税不是这样运作的吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Let's walk through that, OK?
sentences.zh: 我们来理清一下，好吗？

sentences.en: There's a rhyme to the reason why we didn't see that.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到那种现象是有其内在原因的。

sentences.en: I asked him this question a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 我问过他好几次这个问题。

sentences.en: Aren't tariffs supposed to increase prices?
sentences.zh: 难道关税不是应该推高价格吗？

sentences.en: Because that's how tariffs work.
sentences.zh: 因为关税就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: They make the foreign good more expensive, so people buy American goods instead.
sentences.zh: 它们使外国商品更贵，所以人们转而购买美国商品。

sentences.en: But Navarro didn't really give me a direct answer.
sentences.zh: 但纳瓦罗并没有真正给我一个直接的回答。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: We are the biggest market in the world which gives us buying power, OK?
sentences.zh: 我们是世界上最大的市场，这赋予了我们购买力，对吧？

sentences.en: So particularly export-dependent economies, the Chinas of this world, who heavily rely on
sentences.zh: 因此，尤其是那些严重依赖出口的经济体，像中国这样的世界，它们高度依赖

sentences.en: Americans buying their products, if that becomes more difficult to do, what's the first thing these countries are going to do in response to tariffs?
sentences.zh: 美国人购买他们的产品，如果这件事变得更加困难，这些国家面对关税，第一件要做的事会是什么？

sentences.en: What are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: We slap a tariff on.
sentences.zh: 我们加上关税。

sentences.en: What are the producers over there going to do?
sentences.zh: 那边的生产商会怎么做？

sentences.en: What are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: Tell me.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。

sentences.en: What do you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: What would they do?
sentences.zh: 他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: You're a producer over there, and suddenly tariffs are up, and you've got to compete with an American producer.
sentences.zh: 如果你是那边的生产商，突然关税提高了，而你必须与美国生产商竞争。

sentences.en: What are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 你要怎么做？

sentences.en: So your assumption is that they would lower their prices?
sentences.zh: 所以你的假设是他们会降价？

sentences.en: That's exactly what they do.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们会做的。

sentences.en: It's not an assumption.
sentences.zh: 这不是假设。

sentences.en: That's just a fact.
sentences.zh: 这只是事实。

sentences.en: Instead, he talked about how Chinese companies would absorb some of the costs of the tariffs to keep prices low.
sentences.zh: 相反，他谈到中国企业将承担一部分关税成本，以维持低价。

sentences.en: Your goal is to help U.S.
sentences.zh: 你的目标是帮助美国

sentences.en: factories.
sentences.zh: 工厂。

sentences.en: But a lot of U.S.
sentences.zh: 但许多美国

sentences.en: factories do buy components and parts from abroad, and I've talked to a lot of manufacturers who say that would raise their costs.
sentences.zh: 工厂确实从国外购买零部件，我跟许多制造商谈过，他们表示这会增加成本。

sentences.en: It would make them harder for them to make things.
sentences.zh: 这会让他们更难制造产品。

sentences.en: Does that kind of backfire on your agenda?
sentences.zh: 这是否与你的议程适得其反？

sentences.en: So here's one of the iron laws of manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是制造业的铁律之一。

sentences.en: If manufacturing goes abroad, the supply chains follow, and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 如果制造业外流，供应链也会随之而去，反之亦然。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: I also asked him about U.S.
sentences.zh: 我还向他问及了从国外购买零件的美国

sentences.en: manufacturers who are buying parts from abroad, and whether tariffs would hurt their business.
sentences.zh: 制造商，以及关税是否会伤害他们的业务。

sentences.en: And he didn't seem all that concerned with what I've been hearing from some American manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 对于我从一些美国制造商那里听到的担忧，他似乎并不是那么关心。

sentences.en: He just kept coming back to the idea that ultimately, tariffs will incentivize both American and foreign companies to build factories in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他只是不断回到这样一个观点：最终，关税将激励美国和外国公司在美国建设工厂。

sentences.en: You're going to have a domestic investment come quickly when we did the steel...
sentences.zh: 当我们征收钢铁关税时，你会看到国内投资迅速涌入……

sentences.en: Which he believes will then lead to higher wages for Americans.
sentences.zh: 他认为这反过来会为美国人带来更高的工资。

sentences.en: You see wages go up, and that gives consumers more spending power and offsets any rise in prices.
sentences.zh: 你会看到工资上涨，这赋予了消费者更多购买力，并抵消了任何物价上涨。

sentences.en: If real wages rise faster than any other types of inflation, people are still better off.
sentences.zh: 如果实际工资上涨速度快于任何其他类型的通胀，人们的生活依然会更好。

sentences.en: And he said these tariffs aren't happening in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 并且他说这些关税并非在真空中发生。

sentences.en: When I was a campaign advisor in 2016, I had a mantra, right?
sentences.zh: 当我在2016年担任竞选顾问时，我有一个座右铭，对吧？

sentences.en: It was tax cuts, deregulation, strategic energy dominance, fair trade.
sentences.zh: 那就是减税、去监管、战略能源主导地位、公平贸易。

sentences.en: Those were the four components, the tires on the car towards economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 这四大组成部分，就像驶向经济繁荣汽车上的四个轮胎。

sentences.en: He argues that if the Trump administration is able to get the price of oil down, if Elon Musk
sentences.zh: 他认为，如果特朗普政府能够降低油价，如果埃隆·马斯克

sentences.en: and his team are able to cut government waste and red tape, and if Trump keeps taxes low, all of these moves together would reduce inflation and help the U.S.
sentences.zh: 和他的团队能够削减政府浪费和繁文缛节，并且如果特朗普保持低税收，所有这些举措加在一起将减少通胀并帮助美国

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: Because one of the most important things that we're trying to accomplish, that President Trump
sentences.zh: 因为我们要努力实现的最重要事情之一，即特朗普总统

sentences.en: is trying to accomplish is more stable and resilient supply chains, which we have learned to be an enormous problem in the wake of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 正努力实现的是更稳定、更有韧性的供应链，我们在疫情之后认识到这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: So that's a major national security and economic security risk.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个重大的国家安全和经济安全风险。

sentences.en: But what Navarro said is the most important part of all of this, why he's so focused on tariffs
sentences.zh: 但纳瓦罗所说的是这一切中最重要的一部分，他为什么如此专注于关税

sentences.en: and bringing manufacturing back to the United States, is that it all comes back to national security.
sentences.zh: 并将制造业带回美国，归根结底都是为了国家安全。

sentences.en: We get screwed by everyone, and we could afford it in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 我们被所有人占了便宜，我们在20世纪50年代还负担得起。

sentences.en: We can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 我们现在负担不起了。

sentences.en: And that's the thing the rest of the world needs to understand.
sentences.zh: 这就是世界其他地方需要理解的事情。

sentences.en: It's like, when they want to come to Uncle Sam for support, for democracy, if we don't have manufacturing in a defense industrial base, because it all got exported because people
sentences.zh: 这就好像，当他们想向山姆大叔寻求支持、为了民主时，如果我们因为人们

sentences.en: are cheating us on trade, we're not going to be there.
sentences.zh: 在贸易上对我们进行欺诈而导致制造业和国防工业基础全部外流，我们就不会在那里了。

sentences.en: And that's why in the first term, when President Trump said, economic security is national security,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在第一任期内，当特朗普总统说，经济安全就是国家安全时，

sentences.en: it was a very important message and foundation for the way we here in Trump land think about things.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的信息，也是我们这些特朗普阵营的人思考问题的重要基石。

sentences.en: The sense I'm getting from talking to you about your conversation with Navarro is that we're talking about these really aggressive, audacious policy tools.
sentences.zh: 我从与你交流你和纳瓦罗的对话中得到的感觉是，我们在讨论这些非常激进、大胆的政策工具。

sentences.en: And in fact, you know, in some form or fashion, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，以某种形式，美国

sentences.en: has been using them for the past few years.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里一直在使用它们。

sentences.en: They obviously started in the first Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 它们显然始于特朗普的第一届政府。

sentences.en: But what's coming through is that it doesn't sound like Navarro is actually grappling with what you're describing as the potential negative consequences of these tariffs.
sentences.zh: 但传达出来的信息是，纳瓦罗似乎并没有真正认真对待你所描述的这些关税潜在的负面后果。

sentences.en: I don't think that he believes in those negative consequences.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他相信那些负面后果。

sentences.en: No, he doesn't believe in what most experts are saying, which is that all of these tariffs could end up really hurting Americans.
sentences.zh: 不，他不相信大多数专家所说的，即所有这些关税最终可能会真正伤害美国人。

sentences.en: It's not going to be painful for America.
sentences.zh: 这对美国来说不会是痛苦的。

sentences.en: It's going to be a beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 这将是一件美好的事。

sentences.en: President Donald John Trump has proven that tariffs work for the American people.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·约翰·特朗普总统已经证明了关税对美国人民有效。

sentences.en: And they're going to be even more, much more important this second term.
sentences.zh: 在第二任期里，它们将变得更加重要，极其重要。

sentences.en: This is all set in motion now, Ana.
sentences.zh: 这一切现在都已经在启动了，安娜。

sentences.en: So stay tuned.
sentences.zh: 所以请拭目以待。

sentences.en: You know, he and the president are embarking on imposing tariffs at just a vastly bigger scale than we've seen in this country in many decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他和总统正在着手实施几十年未见的、规模庞大的关税。

sentences.en: And so it is kind of like a grand experiment, really, to see if they're right about how tariffs will play out for the American economy.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一个宏大的实验，真的，看看他们关于关税将如何影响美国经济的看法是否正确。

sentences.en: Well, Ana, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，安娜，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: Four top New York City officials are resigning after the Justice Department moved to dismiss the corruption case against Mayor Eric AdaMs.
sentences.zh: 在司法部寻求撤销对埃里克·亚当斯市长的腐败指控后，纽约市四名高官宣布辞职。

sentences.en: The four officials oversee much of the city government, and their departure could further weaken Adams, who's resisting calls to resign.
sentences.zh: 这四位官员监管着大半个市政府，他们的离职可能会进一步削弱亚当斯，而他正拒绝辞职的呼吁。

sentences.en: Adams was indicted on federal bribery and fraud charges, which the DOJ sought to dismiss,
sentences.zh: 亚当斯被联邦贿赂和欺诈罪起诉，司法部寻求撤销起诉，

sentences.en: arguing that the prosecution was politically motivated, and was impeding Adams' ability to cooperate with President Trump's deportation agenda.
sentences.zh: 并辩称该起诉具有政治动机，阻碍了亚当斯配合特朗普总统驱逐出境议程的能力。

sentences.en: And on Monday, a Delta Airlines flight carrying 80 people crashed, flipped over, and injured at least 18 people on board while it was trying to land in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 周一，一架载有80人的达美航空航班在尝试降落多伦多时坠毁、翻覆，造成机上至少18人受伤。

sentences.en: The accident comes after a series of plane crashes over the last few weeks have stoked fears in passengers and raised broader concerns about aviation safety.
sentences.zh: 这起事故发生在一系列飞机失事事件之后，过去几周的事故引发了乘客的恐惧，并引起了对航空安全更广泛的担忧。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Mary Wilson and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由玛丽·威尔逊和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Larissa Anderson, fact-checked by Susan Lee, contains original music by Pat McCusker, Diane Wong, Marion Lozano, and Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周和拉里萨·安德森编辑，苏珊·李核实事实，原创音乐由帕特·麦卡斯克、黛安·王、马里恩·洛扎诺和丹·鲍威尔创作，

sentences.en: and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦贝格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs. See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·亚伯拉罕斯。明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《电线切割机秀》中，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目获取让客人们宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是晕倒才睡着的。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用上或在你喜欢收听的任何地方寻找《电线切割机秀》。
